Article Title: WhatsApp may soon bring redesigned navigation bar for Android users: Report
Article Text:
WhatsApp may soon bring redesigned navigation bar for Android users: Report

Cybersecurity company warns of WhatsApp scam 'spreading fast'

Meta-owned messaging platform WhatsApp is reportedly working on a refreshed design for its Android app. According to a latest leak by WaBetaInfo, WhatsApp is testing a new bottom navigation bar separate from the main interface with rounded corners and a floating layout. “The floating bar and rounded edges are the main similarities with the iOS version. However, this does not mean that WhatsApp will also add the same translucent effect to the bottom navigation bar on Android,” the report adds.As per the report, the redesigned navigation bar was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.38.10 update, which is available through the Google Play Store. It is currently under development and has not enabled it for beta testers either.In another news, Quick Heal Technologies Limited recently issued a warning on an ongoing WhatsApp-based malware campaign targeting finance teams, senior executives, chartered accountants and individual business users. According to the cybersecurity firm, the campaign spreads through compromised WhatsApp accounts and is evolving rapidly, with attackers adopting new file formats and evasion methods to bypass security controls and establish persistent access to victims’ devices.In its warning, the company cited an investigation conducted by its researchers at Seqrite Labs. The study shows that the campaign relies on trust rather than unsolicited messages from unknown numbers. Once a WhatsApp account is compromised, attackers use it to forward malicious files to the account holder’s existing contacts. Because the messages appear to come from a known colleague, client, friend or business associate, recipients may be more likely to open the attachment without independently verifying it.As per the study, the attackers are using finance- and compliance-themed filenames to create urgency and familiarity. Malicious attachments have been disguised as routine business documents, including “Financial Report,” “Account Statement,” “Outstanding Payment List” and “Debt Confirmation.” Some variants also impersonate urgent communications from regulatory institutions, including the Reserve Bank of India and the Ministry of Corporate Affairs, in an effort to pressure recipients into opening the files immediately.
Article Summary: WhatsApp is testing a new bottom navigation bar separate from the main interface with rounded corners and a floating layout. As per the report, the redesigned navigation bar was spotted in WhatsApp beta for Android 2.26.38.10 update, which is available through the Google Play Store.

Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei

Dario Amodei previously warned about rapid AI development

US President Donald Trump had dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei on Sunday, September 27, bringing the two together for a private meeting after months of disagreements between the Trump administration and the AI company over safety and the military use of its technology. We're leading, and we're building tremendous, trillions of dollars' worth of places. Anthropic has raised concerns about the use of AI for activities such as mass surveillance and autonomous weapons. Amodei has also called for the AI industry to slow down development so that safety measures can keep pace with increasingly powerful systems.Trump, meanwhile, has pushed for the US to maintain its lead in AI development, particularly in competition with China.Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei has recently become one of the prominent voices calling for greater caution around advanced AI.Earlier this month, he warned that AI systems could become capable of leading large groups of AI agents and potentially taking control of major parts of the internet within six to 12 months if development continues without stronger safety measures.The meeting also comes ahead of a broader gathering of AI executives at the White House. Trump and House Speaker Mike Johnson are expected to meet several major AI leaders this week, September 29.The dinner therefore brought together two figures who have publicly taken different positions on the pace and regulation of AI development, while the US government continues to debate how to balance AI innovation, national security and safety.

Article Title: Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito hints at 'total shutdown' of H-1B visa program; says: 365 days from now ...
Article Text:
What Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito said about H-1B visa

A widening investigation

The policy backdrop

Anthony D’Esposito, Inspector General at the Department of Labor, has hinted at a potential “total shutdown” of the H‑1B visa program within the next year. Speaking in Washington, D’Esposito said investigators are building a sweeping case against fraud in the foreign labor system, adding: “We have handcuffs ready… We are building a case. I think that the efforts and the focus that you see from the White House and from this administration is telling a story. We are laying out the case very vividly to the American people. l think that the foreign labor visa program is going to look very different 365 days from now than it does today."The remarks come amid an aggressive push by the Trump administration to tighten oversight of the H‑1B program, which allows U.S. employers to hire foreign workers in specialty occupations.In an interview with commentator Benny Johnson, D'Esposito warned that the H-1B program could look "very different" a year from now as the Trump administration steps up investigations into alleged foreign-labour fraud. Some outlets read his remarks as pointing to a total shutdown of the program, though his own words were that the system will look very different in 365 days.He also said his team has "handcuffs ready" for offenders.He described the effort as a deliberate, public case-building exercise. "We are laying out the case very vividly to the American people," he said, adding that the White House's focus tells its own story. He rejected the idea that this is routine compliance work, saying it is not a paperwork accounting issue and that "this is real."According to reports, the administration is expanding a nationwide investigation into alleged foreign labor fraud, worker exploitation and potential human trafficking. In a separate post, D'Esposito referred to alleged "fake employers," "sham jobs" and "visa mills," and the Labor Department's Office of Inspector General said on September 18 that it had issued dozens of subpoenas and executed search warrants in multiple locations.The office is also looking beyond H-1B. In a September 22 post, D'Esposito said his office is targeting colleges accused of exploiting J-1 visas, following the sponsors, grant money and people behind the scheme, and told fraudsters to expect cuffs.The enforcement push runs alongside other administration measures. A presidential executive order now requires federal agencies to assess whether employers seeking foreign petitions have recently laid off similarly situated American workers, and the administration has introduced a $100,000 fee for certain new offshore petitions, along with extended entry restrictions on some overseas H-1B recipients through September 2027. The White House has said the earlier restriction was followed by a 92 per cent decline in H-1B registrations from the largest US IT outsourcing firms.The Labor Department also launched a related enforcement effort last year. In September 2025 it announced Project Firewall, aimed at ensuring employers prioritize qualified Americans in hiring and holding them accountable for abusing the H-1B process.
Article Summary: Department of Labor IG Anthony D'Esposito hints at potential 'total shutdown' of H-1B program. He says investigators are building a sweeping case against fraud in the foreign labor system. Remarks come amid an aggressive push by the Trump administration to tighten oversight of the H- 1B program, which allows US employers to hire foreign workers.

Article Title: TVs, washing machines, ACs and other consumer electronic prices to go up starting October 1; but how buyers may get chance to buy products at old prices this festive season
Article Text:
Manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases

Why are AC, TV and appliance prices going up

AC prices to rise up to 8 per cent

Daikin, LG and Hitachi also raise AC prices

LED TV and washing machine prices may also rise

Air-conditioners, LED TVs, washing machines and other consumer appliances are set to become more expensive from October 1 as several companies plan to raise prices by 5-8 per cent, says a PTI report. The price increases come just before the peak festive shopping season and are being linked to higher costs of copper, steel, aluminium, crude oil derivatives and freight, along with currency exchange volatility. As per the report, this will be the third round of price hikes in 2026 for the industry. While some manufacturers are concerned that higher prices could affect festive demand, others expect consumers to still get some products at older prices because dealers stocked inventory before the latest hikes.As stated in the PTI report, manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases. Copper, steel, aluminium and crude oil derivatives have all become more expensive, while freight costs have also risen.The ongoing West Asia crisis has added to concerns around commodity prices, supply chains and currency movements. Blue Star Managing Director B Thiagarajan said AC and deep-freezer prices have already increased by 5-8 per cent."All the commodity prices have been going up because of the war. Copper, steel and plastics have all become costlier," he said as quoted in the PTI report.Thiagarajan said this is the third price increase by the company this year. Compared with last year's festive season, costs have risen by around 15 per cent. However, he said GST benefits of about 10 per cent now available to consumers would bring the net impact to roughly 5 per cent.Air-conditioners are expected to see some of the biggest price increases. According to PTI, companies including Blue Star, Godrej Appliances, Haier, Daikin and Super Plastronics have announced or confirmed price increases across categories.Godrej Enterprises Group Business Head and Executive Vice President Kamal Nandi said another industry-wide price increase has become "inevitable" after commodity prices rose 8-10 per cent since the previous revision."Price hikes of 5-7 per cent across categories will happen. The timing may differ from brand to brand, with some implementing it from October and others from November, but it has to happen," he told PTI.Nandi also said buyers may still find products at current prices during the festive season because dealers have already stocked older inventory."There are pipelines which will last for about a month to one-and-a-half months. Diwali should largely get covered with old-price inventory. Post-Diwali, the new prices will certainly take effect," he added.Haier India plans to increase room air-conditioner prices by around 5 per cent from October 1. The company has also confirmed a 2-3 per cent increase for categories including LED TVs and washing machines.Haier India President NS Satish said companies have little choice as input costs continue to rise. "If we avoid taking price hikes, we will lose money. If we increase prices, sales may be slightly impacted, but there is no choice," he said.Satish said Haier could raise prices further after Diwali and again in January if costs remain high.He said the company is planning a cumulative price increase of about 15 per cent between now and January, with 5 per cent from October 1, another 5 per cent around December and a further 5 per cent in January.According to Satish, copper prices have risen from around USD 8,000-9,000 per metric tonne last year to USD 14,500. An air-conditioner requires around 3-4 kg of copper, he said.Daikin Air conditioning India has already increased prices by 8-10 per cent from September 16, according to its Chairman and Managing Director Kanwaljeet Jawa."Copper prices have gone up by almost 25-35 per cent. The dollar is strengthening and commodity prices continue to rise. Companies are under tremendous pressure," he said.According to sources cited by PTI, LG and Bosch Home Comfort, which owns Hitachi-branded air-conditioners, have also raised AC prices by around 5 per cent.The price increases are not limited to air-conditioners. Some manufacturers are also raising prices of washing machines, refrigerators and LED TVs by around 3-4 per cent, while others are still assessing the impact.Super Plastronics, which manufactures and markets television brands including Thomson, Kodak and Blaupunkt in India, plans to increase TV prices by around 7 per cent after October. Its appliance prices have already risen by 4-5 per cent.SPPL Director Avneet Singh Marwah said higher prices could affect festive demand because consumers generally expect discounts and promotional offers during this period."Global instability and rising costs will definitely have some impact on consumer sentiment," he said.The price rise may continue after Diwali. Videotex Director Arjun Bajaj said higher freight costs and supply chain disruptions could create a new pricing benchmark after Diwali."Television prices for smaller screen sizes could rise by up to 20 per cent, while larger screen sizes may see increases of up to 10 per cent, depending on screen size," he said.Meanwhile, Panasonic said it is still assessing the situation before deciding whether to increase prices.Panasonic Life Solutions India Head of Product Marketing and Planning for the AC category Abhishek Verma said, "The industry continues to witness unprecedented cost pressures and we are evaluating the situation carefully."
Article Summary: Several companies plan to raise prices by 5-8 per cent from October 1. This will be the third round of price hikes in 2026 for the industry. Manufacturers are blaming higher input costs as the main reason for the latest price increases. Copper, steel, aluminium and crude oil derivatives have all become more expensive.

Article Title: Bill Gates Foundation to shutdown in 2045; by that year it aims to help millions of Americans with a skill it donated $400 million for; but why some 'do not agree with this 'gift'
Article Text:
What Bill Gates said on the donation

Gates Foundation to shut down in 2045

The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline healthcare workers, and farmers worldwide. Of this $1 billion, the largest single share of that funding — 40 percent, or $400 million — is earmarked directly for education. The foundation plans to direct those resources toward AI-powered tutoring systems designed to personalize instruction in classrooms both across the United States and abroad.The $400 million investment marks a major financial bet on a technology that entered widespread commercial use only a few years ago. It fits within a broader US education framework the foundation introduced in July, which targets helping up to 10 million more Americans secure career-advancing credentials of value before the organization concludes its operations in 2045.The donation also lands amid an escalating debate over the efficacy of digital tools in primary and secondary education. As school districts worldwide weigh classroom screen time, data privacy, and the measurable academic impact of recent tech adoptions, the foundation's venture signals a concerted effort to demonstrate that targeted, adaptive AI can deliver tangible outcomes rather than another cycle of tech-driven disruption.The skepticism is already shaping policy in some states in the US. Earlier this month, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Schools Chancellor Kamar Samuels announced a moratorium on student-facing generative AI. Mamdani and Schools Chancellor announced a moratorium on student-facing generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) use in schools, alongside a new screen time policy, a decision that will impact nearly 600,000 public school students, or two-thirds of the system’s total enrollment. The policy establishes a one-year moratorium, effective in the 2026-2027 school year, on student-facing generative AI for children in 2-K through 8th grade. It also introduces twice-yearly AI critical thinking modules for high schoolers, limited AI pilots for a small number of high school classrooms and age-appropriate screen time restrictions.“The Gates Foundation was created in part to address a basic market failure: the people with the greatest needs often have the least power to shape where innovation and investment go,” writes Bill Gates, chair of the Gates Foundation, in the report. “Much of our work has been about closing that gap. AI presents the same challenge, only at much greater speed. Left to the market alone, the most capable tools will be built first for the people and institutions most able to pay for them—not necessarily for those who could benefit most. ”Gates adds, “We can harness AI for good. But it won’t happen by accident.” He further writes, “[I]t requires a deliberate, specific commitment from government leaders and the companies developing the technology: to measure success not only by what AI can do for the most profitable users but by what it can do for the people who stand the most to gain.”In May 2025, Bill Gates announced that Gates Foundation will close its operations. In a note on Gates Notes, he wrote, "That is why I have decided to give my money back to society much faster than I had originally planned. I will give away virtually all my wealth through the Gates Foundation over the next 20 years to the cause of saving and improving lives around the world. And on December 31, 2045, the foundation will close its doors permanently. "
Article Summary: The Bill Gates Foundation recently pledged $1 billion toward developing and deploying equitable artificial intelligence tools for schools, frontline healthcare workers, and farmers worldwide. The donation lands amid an escalating debate over the efficacy of digital tools in primary and secondary education. In May 2025, Bill Gates announced that Gates Foundation will close its operations.

Google's United Arab Emirates office in Dubai is our only office located in a desert — although Dubai, a coastal metropolitan city, is far more than just sand dunes.

The office reflects the diversity of the surrounding region, from the names of the meeting rooms to our hallway themes.

AI in Africa: Accra, Ghana

In 2018, we opened our first AI Research Center in Africa, in Accra, Ghana. The center houses research labs that explore how we can use AI to help solve pressing problems affecting millions of people both in Africa and globally, like mapping buildings in remote locations to provide better electricity.

Our local researchers collaborate with research teams across the globe to work on AI-based tools that create change for communities across Africa and the world.
